founder: Pieter Levels (via Remote OK) + Web3 Jobs team — site footer: 'by Web3 Jobs + Remote OK'; Remote OK is Levels' bootstrapped job board

category: AI recruiting / applicant-screening micro-SaaS (AI ATS pre-filter)
targetCustomer: Founders and hiring managers flooded with AI-generated, look-alike job applications (notably web3/remote startups).
customerSegment: Small B2B: startups and SMBs hiring high-volume roles; named users include SideShift, Umbrel, Rug AI, Blade Labs, Zircuit.
coreProblem: AI-written resumes and cover letters all look identical, burying the few high-quality applicants in hundreds of look-alikes.
problemFrequency: Per hiring round: hundreds of applications per posting must be triaged in days.
problemSeverity: HIGH for the buyer (wrong/slow hires are expensive) but the screening step itself is MEDIUM — a time-sink, not existential.
existingAlternatives: Greenhouse, Lever, Workable (positioned as complement: pre-filter before ATS), manual CV review, other AI resume screeners.
currentUserWorkflow: Founder/recruiter manually opens every CV and cover letter, or lets them pile up in an ATS inbox and hires whoever surfaced first.
productSolution: AI pre-screening layer: custom application form with screening questions; AI scores every applicant and only high scorers reach the ATS; auto-rejection emails.
coreFeature: AI applicant scoring + ATS gating (score threshold redirects only the best into Greenhouse/Lever/Workable) plus a free built-in ATS.
initialMVP: AI scoring form + ATS redirect flow (current landing page centers entirely on this single job: score, filter, pass best to ATS).
featuresNotInMVP: Full built-in ATS (unlimited jobs, branded career page, pipeline stages) — framed on-site as an added layer, suggesting it followed the scorer.
currentFeatureSet: AI scoring, custom hidden instructions, strengths/weaknesses view, applicant import, auto-rejection templates, free ATS (jobs, career page, pipeline stages, interview invites), ATS integrations.
pricingModel: Paid-only tiered SaaS by open-job count; no free plan, no trial — 14-day refund instead.
pricingTiers: Pro $99/mo (2 open jobs); Premium $199/mo (10 jobs, most popular); Enterprise $299/mo (20 jobs, embeds, dedicated support).
freeTier: None for AI screening; a free built-in ATS tier is advertised ('What you can do with our free ATS').

devMethod: UNKNOWN for this product; Levels' documented method is solo build-in-public, tiny single-file codebases.

productComplexity: LOW — one job (screen faster) with a free-ATS wedge.

competitiveMoat: Distribution moat (Remote OK/Web3 Jobs applicant flow) + founder audience; product itself is thin and replicable.
competitors: Greenhouse, Lever, Workable (incumbent ATS), Covey Scout, CloudApper AI Recruiter, AIApply, ResumeScreening.ai.
competitiveWeaknesses: Thin product (a scoring prompt + form) vs full-platform ATS suites; no public traction proof; enterprise HR prefers incumbents.
retention: UNKNOWN — usage is episodic per hiring round; churn dynamics NOT PUBLIC.

notCopy: Do not clone without equivalent applicant-flow distribution; the product is trivially replicable and employment-AI bias scrutiny is rising.

mainDistribution: UNKNOWN — distribution never identified as the problem; thesis failure preceded scale questions.

operationalComplexity: LOW — and still failed: proves failure was thesis, not execution.

competitiveMoat: NONE — the postmortem's central point; incumbent (ChatGPT Workspace Agents) later absorbed the surface entirely.
competitors: ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Poe, and every model-router clone; Builder.ai cited as same-shape failure ($1.2B → bankruptcy May 2025).
competitiveWeaknesses: Total: no model ownership, no workflow lock-in, no specific user; commoditized from both sides (models below, incumbents above).
retention: 'Churn was tolerable' (founder) — retention was FINE and the product still died; the lab's key counterexample to retention-as-health.
legalPrivacy: N/A (dead); multi-provider data-passing would have been the live risk.
monetizationDifficulty: FATAL — no margin to defend once routing value → 0; 'aggregator products in commoditising markets do not scale' (verbatim lesson).
zeroUpfront: NO — lesson-grade: inference-arbitrage wrappers carry per-query API costs with zero pricing power; the category cannot self-fund.
mrr100: LOW — failed the scaling-potential test by founder verdict; each new user routed to the same models, opening no new jobs.
learn: WHAT WENT WRONG: foundation-model convergence (GPT-4-class = floor by late 2024) killed the routing premise; 'working + tolerable churn' masked structural non-viability; kill threshold should have been Nov 2024, not Mar 2025. Rule: if your moat is 'we choose,' it dies when choice flattens.
notCopy: Do not build model routers/aggregators on commoditising intelligence; build specific tools that solve one user's problem 10x (the Gravity pivot: deployer, not aggregator).

growthEvidence: No growth figures; category context: 'AI companion was the deadliest AI vertical of 2025' (TechStartups Dec 2025, cited by founder).

aiUsage: Generative companion dialogue with memory/check-ins; compute-heavy by design (long contextual turns).
devMethod: Small-team build + spreadsheet-driven kill decision (Jan 2026 price experiments → Feb shutdown).

technicalComplexity: LOW-MEDIUM — chat + memory plumbing; the hard part was economics, not engineering.
productComplexity: MEDIUM — personality system + memory + check-ins that 'felt like remembering.'

retention: Week-one strong → week-three crash ('loved week one, forgotten by week three'); retention curve + cost curve crossed before revenue converged.
legalPrivacy: Companion-data sensitivity (disclosure-heavy chats, minors risk) is the category's live legal wire; details NOT REVIEWED (dead product).
acquisitionDifficulty: LOW (demand was real) — which made the trap worse: growth deepened losses.
monetizationDifficulty: FATAL — 'no price the audience would accept covered compute cost' (paraphrase of founder's 90-day cohort verdict).
zeroUpfront: NO — lesson-grade: long-context consumer inference at low subscription prices = structurally negative margin; subsidies only delay shutdown.
mrr100: LOW — failed the sustainable-margins test by founder verdict; 'there is no scale-to-margin path from negative unit economics.'
learn: WHAT WENT WRONG: per-active-user compute cost exceeded audience willingness-to-pay at every tested price; week-one engagement masked week-three retention collapse; 'maybe scale fixes it' delayed kill from month ~3 signal to month 9. Rule: set a cost-per-user kill threshold on calendar; engagement is not a business.
notCopy: Do not build flat-subscription companion apps on long-context inference; if entering, use compute-aware pricing (per-outcome/capability) or a B2B payer (wellness/benefits) — each is a different startup, per founder.
